evidence: Scaling estimate by load equivalence with observed Earth aggregates; no measured strength of a decimetre aggregate, no resolved lunar turbulence.
assumptions: The weakest junction carries a load that grows with the flake, and its strength does not depend on the flake's size; lunar and Earth flakes are built from similar crystals and contacts.
The largest observed Earth flakes are taken to sit at their strength limit; growth time or water may limit them instead, which would make the lunar spans conservative.
Lunar flakes spend one to four days aloft: contacts sinter and strengthen (Demmenie et al. 2025), while repeated sublimation can loosen them (Oraltay and Hallett 1989); neither is quantified.
The turbulent fluctuation is linearized in du/V; a lunar dissipation rate is unmeasured, so it is varied from a tenth to ten times Earth's.
